title: Accelerating Gravitational N-Body Simulations Using the RISC-V-Based Tenstorrent Wormhole
problem: N-body astrophysical simulations computationally expensive; traditional CPUs have limited throughput. RISC-V accelerators emerging but validation needed for scientific computing workloads.
motivation: RISC-V-based accelerators (Tenstorrent Wormhole) originally designed for AI workloads but may suit scientific computing. Astrophysical N-body simulations competitive benchmark for alternative accelerators.
method: The researchers adapted astrophysical N-body simulation code (software that calculates gravitational forces between many objects like stars or planets) to run on a Tenstorrent Wormhole n300 accelerator card—a specialized piece of hardware based on RISC-V architecture (a simple, open instruction set for chips) instead of traditional CPUs. They then benchmarked the accelerator against a highly optimized CPU baseline to measure how much faster it could perform the same calculations.
key_novelty: This work shows that the RISC-V-based Tenstorrent Wormhole accelerator can handle scientific computing workloads, demonstrated through astrophysical N-body simulations.
contributions: >2× speedup vs highly optimized CPU implementation
Demonstrates RISC-V accelerator viability for scientific computing
N-body simulation as competitive benchmark for emerging accelerators
limitations: No comparison with GPU accelerators or other RISC-V variants
primary_theme: RISC-V accelerator validation for scientific computing
